sections.html: The males stop growing at a total length of about 6 cm, but the females can grow up to about 10 cm.

Most halfbeaks of the genus Nomorhamphus originate from Sulawesi (formerly known as Celebes). Some species, like N. ebrardtii or N. rex, are usually traded as wild-collected fish, while others, among them N. liemi, are occasionally also available as bred fish. A species that hardly ever occurs in the trade is the Black Halfbeak, Nomorhamphus celebensis. Currently some German-bred fish are available.
This species is not as colourful as others, but comparatively very peaceful. It tolerates both conspecifics and other species in the tank.
During display behaviour the males of N. celebensis become jet-black. Males stop growing at about 6 cm total length, while females reach about 10 cm.

When breeding these fish, the basic task is to save the offspring, as the parents are cannibalistic. A gravid female must never be separated too late, as she will often give birth to dead young. She must also not be separated too early, because these fish are quite lively and need free space for swimming. So even breeding these "simple" livebearers is quite tricky.
